question: What type of lens does the upper part of the bi-focal lens have?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Presbyopia:

 
 
• The power of accommodation of the eye decreases with aging.
 
• People with the defect can't see nearby as well as distant objects distinctly.
 
• Causes - (a) gradual weakening of ciliary muscles, (b) diminishing flexibility of the eye lens.
 
• Correction - **bi-focal lenses**, in which the** upper portion consists** of the **concave lens** (facilitates **distant vision**) and the **lower portion consists** of the **convex lens** (facilitates **near vision**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prism:**
 
• 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11866c472f9664763858d0d83a5f29d9464048fc1bb51520cd4d621e99ad1a20.png] 

 
 
• The splitting of a composite beam of light into its constituent colors is called dispersion of light.
 
• The dispersion of white light occurs because the colors of white light travel at different speeds through the glass prism.
 
• The dispersion was discovered by Sir Issac Newton.
 
• Newton discovered that light is made up of seven different colors.
